structures.name: Left cephalic vein
structures.description: Superficial vein on the lateral forearm and arm; a common peripheral IV site.

structures.name: Left basilic vein
structures.description: Superficial vein on the medial forearm; with the median cubital vein it forms the antecubital IV/venepuncture site.

structures.name: Left superficial epigastric artery
structures.description: Superficial artery of the lower abdominal wall.

structures.name: Left iliotibial tract
structures.description: Thick band of fascia on the lateral thigh.

structures.name: Left flexor retinaculum
structures.description: Roof of the carpal tunnel.

structures.name: Right flexor retinaculum

structures.name: Right medial brachial vein
structures.description: Vein accompanying the brachial artery.

structures.name: Heart (myocardium)
structures.description: Four-chamber pump. The left ventricle (tinted when ischaemic in the simulation) generates systemic pressure; the right ventricle perfuses the lungs.

structures.name: Coronary arteries
structures.description: Supply the myocardium. Occlusion of the left anterior descending (LAD) artery causes anterior infarction.

structures.name: Cardiac veins
structures.description: Drain the myocardium into the right atrium via the coronary sinus.

structures.name: Aorta
structures.description: Main systemic artery. Mean arterial pressure in the simulation refers to pressure here.

structures.name: Venae cavae & brachiocephalic veins
structures.description: Return blood to the right atrium. Raised intrathoracic pressure (tension pneumothorax, high PEEP) impedes venous return.

structures.name: Azygos & hemiazygos veins
structures.description: Drain the posterior thoracic wall into the superior vena cava.

structures.name: Pulmonary trunk & arteries
structures.description: Carry deoxygenated blood from the right ventricle to the lungs.

structures.name: Pulmonary veins
structures.description: Return oxygenated blood to the left atrium; raised left atrial pressure causes pulmonary oedema.

structures.name: Carotid, subclavian & vertebral arteries
structures.description: Supply the brain and upper limbs; the carotid pulse is checked here.

structures.name: Left upper-limb arteries
structures.description: Brachial, radial and ulnar arteries. The radial pulse is lost at low systolic pressure; arterial lines are placed in the radial artery.

structures.name: Left iliac & lower-limb arteries
structures.description: Iliac, femoral and leg arteries. The femoral pulse is palpated below the inguinal ligament.

structures.name: Left iliac veins
structures.description: Drain the pelvis and lower limb into the inferior vena cava.

structures.name: Right upper-limb arteries
structures.description: Brachial, radial and ulnar arteries. The radial pulse is lost at low systolic pressure; arterial lines are placed in the radial artery.

structures.name: Right iliac & lower-limb arteries
structures.description: Iliac, femoral and leg arteries. The femoral pulse is palpated below the inguinal ligament.

structures.name: Right iliac veins
structures.description: Drain the pelvis and lower limb into the inferior vena cava.

structures.name: Visceral arteries
structures.description: Supply the gut, liver, spleen and kidneys; splanchnic vasoconstriction diverts blood in shock.

structures.name: Hepatic portal vein
structures.description: Carries gut venous blood to the liver (first-pass metabolism of oral drugs).

structures.name: Trachea
structures.description: Windpipe; an endotracheal tube cuff sits in the mid-trachea. Tracheal deviation is a late sign of tension pneumothorax.

structures.name: Main bronchi
structures.description: The right main bronchus is steeper — a tube advanced too far enters it.

structures.name: Left bronchial tree
structures.description: Conducting airways; bronchospasm narrows them (wheeze, prolonged expiration).

structures.name: Right bronchial tree
structures.description: Conducting airways; bronchospasm narrows them (wheeze, prolonged expiration).

structures.name: Left lung
structures.description: Two lobes plus the lingula. In the simulation it collapses as pleural air accumulates on this side.

structures.name: Right lung
structures.description: Three lobes. In the simulation it collapses as pleural air accumulates on this side.

structures.name: Diaphragm
structures.description: Principal muscle of inspiration; it descends with each breath (animated from the simulated tidal volume).

structures.name: Oesophagus
structures.description: Lies behind the trachea — oesophageal intubation produces no chest rise and no end-tidal CO₂.

structures.name: Stomach
structures.description: Gastric insufflation during bag-mask ventilation raises aspiration risk.

structures.name: Duodenum
structures.description: First part of the small intestine.

structures.name: Jejunum
structures.description: Absorptive small intestine.

structures.name: Ileum
structures.description: Terminal small intestine.

structures.name: Appendix
structures.description: Vermiform appendix (right iliac fossa).

structures.name: Colon
structures.description: Large intestine.

structures.name: Rectum
structures.description: Terminal large intestine.

structures.name: Liver
structures.description: Metabolises lactate and many drugs; hepatic clearance in the simulation falls with liver blood flow and hepatic impairment.

structures.name: Gallbladder
structures.description: Stores bile beneath the liver.

structures.name: Pancreas
structures.description: Endocrine β-cells secrete insulin; absent insulin secretion drives diabetic ketoacidosis in the simulation.

structures.name: Left cerebral hemisphere
structures.description: Cerebral cortex and white matter; consciousness falls with cerebral hypoperfusion, hypoxaemia, hypoglycaemia and sedative drugs.

structures.name: Right cerebral hemisphere
structures.description: Cerebral cortex and white matter; consciousness falls with cerebral hypoperfusion, hypoxaemia, hypoglycaemia and sedative drugs.

structures.name: Cerebellum
structures.description: Coordinates movement and balance.

structures.name: Brainstem
structures.description: Contains the respiratory centres; opioids depress the medullary response to CO₂.

structures.name: Hypothalamus & pineal
structures.description: The hypothalamus sets the thermoregulatory set-point (raised by pyrogens in sepsis).

structures.name: Spinal cord
structures.description: Conducts motor and sensory signals; it ends at about L1–L2 in adults.

structures.name: Left kidney
structures.description: Filters plasma; glomerular filtration in the simulation falls when renal perfusion pressure drops below autoregulation.

structures.name: Right kidney
structures.description: Filters plasma; glomerular filtration in the simulation falls when renal perfusion pressure drops below autoregulation.

structures.name: Ureters
structures.description: Carry urine to the bladder.

structures.name: Urinary bladder
structures.description: Urine output is a key marker of end-organ perfusion.

structures.name: Adrenal glands
structures.description: Secrete adrenaline and cortisol — the endogenous stress response.

structures.name: Thymus
structures.description: Lymphoid organ in the anterior mediastinum (small in adults).

structures.name: Pituitary gland
structures.description: Releases ADH (conserves water in hypovolaemia) and ACTH.
